label: Analytical termination in primary…: Monadology §§33–35 proposes resolving necessary truths into…
definition: Monadology §§33–35 proposes resolving necessary truths into simpler ideas and truths, ending in primary identity principles whose opposites expressly contradict. This is Leibniz’s account of reasons for necessary truths, not a general finite-causal-history requirement or a license for arbitrary unproved starting points.
